learningObjectives: Create a testing strategy covering important application layers.
Identify documentation required for a production-ready Java project.
Select optimization and quality improvements based on application requirements.

activities.title: Testing Strategy
activities.instruction: Explore how different tests cover different application boundaries.

content.concept: A capstone testing strategy can combine unit tests for isolated logic, integration tests for component boundaries, API tests for HTTP behavior, and end-to-end tests for important user journeys.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Test individual classes or methods in isolation.
Verify that multiple application components work together correctly.
Verify HTTP endpoints, request handling, responses, and API behavior.
Validate complete user workflows across the application.

activities.title: Choose the Test Type
activities.instruction: Choose the test type that best matches the scenario.

content.concept: The appropriate test depends on the boundary being validated and the behavior that needs to be verified.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Testing one service method with mocked dependencies → Unit Test
Testing the complete registration journey through the UI → End-to-End Test
Testing a controller endpoint through HTTP → API Test
Testing repository and database interaction together → Integration Test
config.answer: Testing one service method with mocked dependencies → Unit Test

content.concept: A production-ready Java application should address functional testing, security, configuration, error handling, observability, documentation, and deployment verification.

activities.title: Performance Investigation
activities.instruction: Explore the main areas that can affect Java application performance.

content.concept: Performance optimization should be based on observed bottlenecks. Common investigation areas include database queries, algorithms, network calls, memory usage, and application configuration.
